a.text: In the corner of every session is a figure with her head perpetually down, recording every word said by the City Council.

steps.text: January 1st, 10:12 A.M.
'We propose waiving the right to education for the Infected.'
'We propose imposing no limit on the hours an Infected can work, to ensure that they can earn as much as their ability allows, supporting their own livelihood.'
'We urge the Infected to wear special Infected clothing going forward...'
The silent recorder moves her sore wrists, turning to a new page in her notebook.
January 8th, 6:23 P.M.
'Councilor Jones objects, and proposes a new criteria for assigning jobs to the Infected...'
'Councilor Moneywell proposes a bill to limit the number of Infected factories can employ...'

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Still busy, Kite?

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Mhm...

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Sorry to bother you, but may I ask... where exactly are those documents regarding the demolition of the factories in the east end filed? I can't find them at all.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Folder no.10289 in cabinet B03, third drawer behind the bookshelf.

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Heh, I just knew you'd know where it was right away! If I had a head as good as yours, my mum would be so happy she'd slurp down three bowls of cheese soup at once!

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Work hours are already over though, so why's your pen still moving...? Oh, Infected this, Infected that... my head hurts.

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: I already sent in an application; even if I'm just a receptionist for the council chamber, it'd still be better than being a filing clerk. This is just too boring! Why not try applying too, Kite? We can work there together.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: What? No no no!

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: You don't know how hard I worked for this recorder job. My parents want me to be safe and secure, so keeping this position is the best for me. How could I even think of transferring?

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Gosh, you're just too timid!

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: *sigh* Come on, just look at this pot of half-withered flowers I've been raising. Even if I were to change jobs, their situation probably wouldn't get any better.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: My brain's good at rote memorization, so being a recorder suits me just fine.
January 15th, 11:45 A.M.
'We propose issuing a special series of banknotes for the Infected, to boost domestic demand...'
'We propose issuing half of the Infected's wages in the form of consumer vouchers...'

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Phew......

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Wait, I have one more bill to propose!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: As I'm sure we all saw this morning, the protest march against Infected desegregation has become such a nuisance that it's even blocking the roads that some of us councilors take!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: I was in a hurry and had to loudly heckle them several times to stop blocking my way to work, lest today's council session be delayed.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: So I propose allowing the Infected to buy homes, what does everyone think?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: If all those Infected workers had adequate housing, they would stop wandering about like vagrants looking for shelter. Then they wouldn't have any reason to interfere with the lives of ordinary people and spark such protests, yes?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Additionally, there are quite a number of Infected in Caladon these days. If each of them bought a house, imagine the boost to the economy!

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Councilor Jones, I hear from the others that you've taken on the bid for that land development project on the east end, and they were all harping on about how it was a huge project that would take at least a decade to finish.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Hey now! That's all just hearsay, how could you possibly believe that... Besides, how could it be compared to the roadwork you're backing?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Once the roads are good as new, the people will get moving, and then anything and everything could happen, right?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Our city's development is progressing at a steady pace, but there's no place for such protests in our future. Just a few of us were delayed today, but who knows how much worse it could be tomorrow?

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Keeping the general public of Caladon safe and earning their trust is our most basic responsibility.

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Only once the residents are at ease can we think about developing our economy!

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Recorder? Did you get all that down?

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Yes, Miss Councilor.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: So, what does everyone think? As soon as the road connecting to the east end is repaired, we can begin work on so many more projects!

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: ...I have no particular opinion on this, but such a bill will be beneficial to everyone, so I will back your proposal.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Recorder, be sure to note every word of this down! The quicker we settle this, the better!

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Got it, Councilor Jones.

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor
steps.text: Please hold on for a moment. I have something to say about the previous proposal.

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor
steps.text: I find myself curious. These Infected workers... would they even be able to afford a house?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Whyever not? They'll earn enough from the roadwork, and it'll all sort itself out.
January 15th, 6:12 P.M.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: So, the good news is that the processing of both the business certificates and access permits the landship needs is going well, so you'll be able to get them all by the next month.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: And the bad news is that in the six months since you last submitted a report, it's been long enough for them to finally make a little breakthrough on their proposed bills.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: And this latest one is to 'let the Infected buy houses'?

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: ...If I recall your last report correctly, you mentioned that there were a couple of bills proposed that were potentially beneficial for the Infected. What happened to those?

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: You can probably come up with an answer to that yourself, Captain.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: The councilors feel that even though this one is the least feasible, it can still be taken advantage of. Whether it be by those holding vacant land, those with factories, or those repairing the roads, they all want a piece of the pie.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Now that the bill has already been placed on the cutting board, all that's left is to divide the pie to everybody's satisfaction.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: The remaining proposals will be squished under the pie pan, and maybe trod upon a few more times for good measure.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: ...I know that much.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Recently, we've been admitting more Infected patients with acute symptoms.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: I'm not complaining, but... things are getting harder for us, even with all the material support we're getting from the landship.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: And there will only be more such patients in the future.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: That said... the certificates and permits you're getting us will give us more options. So we might still have some tricks up our sleeve going forward.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: But... gah! Do you know what kind of Infected we've been admitting this month? Children!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Our efforts will be for naught if they keep screwing around in their City Council sessions like this!

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: ...But we can't interfere, right?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Yes, generally speaking.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Captain, what do you think about Skyfire?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Why bring her up all of a sudden?

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Oh, I was just... I think she comes from a good background, and has a good heart, but her worldview is still a little small.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: She listens to reason, but has never had to experience reality, so she used an improper method to deal with those councilors when she found out how they really are.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: If not for Councilor Angst, or her identity as a Mountbelan, those nobles probably would have served her a lesson—both overt and covert—and forced her out of Caladon in disgrace.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Sometimes she disagrees with my methods too. I'll always choose to preserve my status as a City Council recorder first, mindlessly nodding my head and noting down whatever the councilors say.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Only occasionally do I bring you the evidence they leave behind to make some use out of it.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: I always thought her way of charging into things head-on was no good, but—

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: She's never made an error, and never forgets it: what she does is right. She has never relented on this.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: We all have our own ways of upholding justice, Kazemaru.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Hah... But the councilors usually take no notice of me. They don't even remember my name.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: They just go 'Recorder, record this,' 'Recorder, take that down.' They probably wouldn't even notice if I changed into a completely different person one day.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Kazemaru, we can't interfere with the council.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: I used to chide Skyfire for that too, saying she shouldn't do such a rash thing.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: ...You know your limits.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Of course I do. So I'm going to pack up my things and go back to the archives and continue sorting through the files.

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Oh right, these are the little paper animals I folded. You can give them to the younger Infected to play with.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Now that's more like it. Don't look so sad, we're still hanging in there. We'll manage to figure something out.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: ...Wait, why do these look so much rougher than the ones from last time?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Look at this horn, it's all twisted! It better not turn into a one-winged fowlbeast when I give it to a kid later!

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: ...I'm going now!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: *sigh*
January 17th, 7:19 A.M.

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Early day today, Kite?

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: A new batch of documents arrived, so I'm sorting and filing them...

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Oh, I heard you got transferred to the front desk? Congrats!

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Heheh, it's my last day today here, so I'll help you out!

steps.name: Recorder Colleague
steps.text: Let me tell you, I was passing by the council room yesterday, and I heard them argue about whether to raise the tax rate to limit the Infected's quality of life... even I thought that was a bit of a joke.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Yeah.
January 22nd, 7:32 A.M.
'We propose deducting 30% of the Infected's wages as a reparations fee, to pay for the damages caused to the city by the Infected.'
'We propose following Columbia's example, for the wilderness has vast acres of untapped resources with which the Infected may live prosperous lives.'
The recorder in the corner puts down her pen and, as if having gotten dust on them, wipes her hands vigorously with a handkerchief from her pocket before throwing it into the nearby trashcan.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: ...Ssh!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: What's wrong with you? Don't make so much noise all of a sudden! Don't recorders know such a basic rule?

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: ...My apologies, Councilor Jones.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: I will make sure to stay quiet.
January 27th, 6:42 P.M.
'We will continue to push for the bill to let the Infected buy housing...'
'We expect it to be implemented by next year...'
The recorder organizes the documents, carefully filing them into their respective envelopes, and writes the date on the label before placing them into the filing cabinet.
There is a thin layer of dust on top of the cabinet, and she picks up a rag and wipes it.
She turns to her desk and begins to tidy up the area—the Records Room is packed with people looking for information during the day, and keeping the desk neat and tidy is also part of her disguise.
A potted flower sits on the corner of the desk, its petals drooping.
*crash*—!
An unstable flower pot is buffeted by the wind and falls from the sky, throwing streaks of soil and scattering petals everywhere.
The clay pot falls straight down with the mud and hits a young woman just passing by square on her head.
She does not let out any kind of cry after her collision, but simply touches the mud on her face in a daze.
The recorder looks at the pot of dropping flowers on her desk, which she had just tended to earlier, and finds its position perfectly secure.
She stretches a hand out.
*crash*—!
January 27th, 10:39 P.M.

steps.name: Lamenting Voice
steps.text: Aaaahhhhhh—!!

steps.name: Amazed Passerby
steps.text: What was that?! Did you hear that? Was that even human? That gave me a real fright!

steps.name: Apathetic Passerby
steps.text: The whole of Caladon probably heard that scream.

steps.name: Apathetic Passerby
steps.text: It sounded like it came from the villas. Maybe the nobles are playing around with some new toys again.

steps.name: Amazed Passerby
steps.text: Whew, that ding dong clanging sure sounded like someone waltzing around with furniture strapped onto their back!

steps.name: Apathetic Passerby
steps.text: Haha, a waltz with furniture? How posh!

Ten minutes ago, Councilor Jones had been lounging comfortably on his sofa, sipping the wine his servants had prepared for him. Their backs blended into the light, while the shadows of his guards were reflected at his feet.
In Caladon, such an arrangement allows him to enjoy many a perfectly peaceful night in his mansion.
But few things are absolute.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Ah—Ahh—!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: What is this, what's happening?!
The books on the shelf and the medals on the wall all stand up, taking even the bookshelf straight towards the couch where the councilor is lounging.
As if alive, a bunch of paper folds itself, becoming tiny figures, mouths, sharp knives.
They swirl around the confused councilor—

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Help! Someone, help! What's all this!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: My books? My... files? They're alive!
The paper dolls vibrate in mid-air, and tiny voices seep out from the words written on them—

steps.name: Paper Doll
steps.text: 'We urge the Infected to wear special Infected clothing going forward!'

steps.name: Paper Mouth
steps.text: 'We propose issuing a special series of banknotes for the Infected, to boost domestic demand!'

steps.name: Paper Knife
steps.text: 'Let them buy housing? Yes, of course! Let them buy houses, we have many uses for the Infected!'

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Ahhh!!! What's going on, someone! Anyone? Guards? Guards!

steps.name: Paper Doll
steps.text: 'Cystymilk is delicious, and we should increase our supply! The Infected—'

steps.name: Paper Mouth
steps.text: 'The Infected should pay a reparations fee! We propose issuing half of the Infected's wages in the form of consumer vouchers!'

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: What are these! Get, get away from me!
The Councilor falls to the ground on his back, flailing his hands in an attempt to drive away the paper dolls encircling him.
He picks up a wine glass, aiming its contents at a paper doll. The wine seeps into the paper, and the swirl of white turns red as it fills the room with an alcoholic aroma.
Head in hands, the councilor huddles in a corner of the room, leaving only his rotund backside shaking in view.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Ah! Ahh!! AHHH!!
The paper dolls continue to close in on him, the overlapping voices encircling the Councilor.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Who are you? What do you want?!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: W-What, what do you want from me?!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: I'll do anything you ask! Anything! Let me go, just let me go, please?!
As if they had gotten what they wanted, the paper dolls stop spinning around the councilor and instead hover quietly.
Then, they stretch out their bodies, reverting to their original sheets of paper before landing on the ground. The councilor panics and crumples them, afraid that they might once again take flight.
In the midst of the flurry, a document lands quietly on the middle of his desk.
His hands trembling, Councilor Jones picks it up—

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: 'Report on the City's East End Development Project'...?

After glancing at the open document for just a few seconds, the councilor crumples it into a ball with a twisted expression on his face. He is about to throw it into the trash, but hesitantly smooths it out instead, folds it, and carefully places it in his inner coat pocket.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: This... What is this doing here...? Who found this? Didn't I already...

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: Sir... did you call for me? Should I come in and help you clean up?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: You dolt! What are you standing outside for!

steps.name: Bodyguard
steps.text: R-Right away!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Wait... No! No need!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Out! Get out! Get away from here, now!
The councilor bends down and scrambles to gather the papers scattered on the floor, fearfully scanning the heading and contents of each sheet, as if afraid to see something else on them.
He looks around, wary of the entire room. He then pulls back the curtains with a flourish.
Someone is definitely behind this! And he's going to find out who!
Ah, if it isn't Councilor Jones? Still at work at such a late hour, tidying up your papers?

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: You?!

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor's Voice
steps.text: (Loudly) I expected no less of you, Councilor Jones! To still be hard at work sorting through your files at such a late hour, polishing your proposal into an even better bill to better serve everyone!

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor's Voice
steps.text: (Loudly) I just now finished discussing the east end factory with the Infected representative earlier, and he's so grateful to see you working so hard for the council!

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor's Voice
steps.text: (Loudly) Truly a councilor who looks after the Infected! Come come, representative, you must thank him in person!

steps.name: Infected Representative's voice
steps.text: Truly, thank you so much, Councilor Jones! Our brothers in the factories will surely remember you for this!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: ...Haha, hahaha.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Y-Yes, yes! Haha...!
February 3rd, 9:19 P.M.

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Councilor Jones, withdrawing a proposal is unprecedented. Do you realize what your actions are implying?

steps.name: Calm Councilor
steps.text: Everyone here has been working hard on their own preparations these last few days, all based on that proposal.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: ...No, I'm saying... I... I want to withdraw that bloody proposal!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Please forgive me, I... I've come to my senses over the last few days. This was a foolish idea.

steps.name: Extremely Serious Councilor
steps.text: Councilor Jones, the City Council is no place for playing around. Perhaps if you told us of any difficulties you've encountered recently, we might be able to help you.

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: No! Nothing of the sort!

steps.name: Emotional Councilor
steps.text: Recorder? Recorder, are you there? Kite, Kite! Quick, note down my decision to withdraw the proposal! And file it! Quickly!
The recorder clicks her pencil, and as per her usual, writes down every word from the session in her minutes.

steps.name: Kite the Recorder
steps.text: Got it, Councilor Jones.
February 7th, 3:18 P.M.

steps.name: Curious Voice
steps.text: What a pity I went home early that night. Who would've expect something like that to happen in Councilor Jones's own home?

steps.name: Excited Voice
steps.text: I've heard others say that the house was completely fine, but suddenly the stationery started moving and dancing. It could even speak!

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Here are the business certifications and permits. You can return to the landship now, captain.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Good job on your end, too.

steps.name: Curious Voice
steps.text: I heard his servants say that the councilor was frightened by something, but he didn't let them or even his guards enter the room. He tidied up his room himself!

steps.name: Excited Voice
steps.text: I also heard that ever since that day, the Jones family has forbidden the use of paper, saying that some kind of foul evil lies within, haha! Then, how do you think he does his business in the loo...?

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Seems like they're talking about what happened to Councilor Jones the other day? News spreads so fast, doesn't it?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: ...*cough*!

steps.name: Curious Voice
steps.text: Hey, enough about this, the captain's still hard at work so we should be too!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Kazemaru.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Did you...?

steps.name: Excited Voice
steps.text: Captain, do you have the inside story? Share it with us, we won't tell a soul!

steps.name: Kazemaru
steps.text: Ssh.
